subject: Webhook integration delay — request for trial extension and interim credits
messages:
From: Eli Chen <eli.chen@fastpay.io>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Webhook verification failing during onboarding

Hi Laura,

We're running into a blocker during FastPay's integration with the Redwood webhook endpoint. Our engineering team is seeing a TLS/certificate mismatch when Redwood attempts to POST to our callback URL, and the retries from our side are causing duplicated events in our sandbox. That means our QA run for the pilot is stalled.

Can you help with two things:
1) A 30-day trial extension so we don't lose our pilot window while we debug;
2) A small sandbox credit (we're asking for $2k) to cover extra token consumption while we re-run QA once the callback is stable.

I've attached the webhook logs that show the handshake failures (webhook_logs.txt). Our team is ready to pair with one of your engineers to get this resolved quickly. ETA from our side is uncertain until we confirm the root cause; right now we expect it might take 3-7 business days.

Thanks for the help — we're excited to get Redwood integrated.

Best,
Eli Chen
Head of Integrations, FastPay
eli.chen@fastpay.io
ops@fastpay.io

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Eli Chen <eli.chen@fastpay.io>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Webhook verification failing during onboarding — quick triage notes

Thanks for the ping, Laura. I pulled the webhook_logs.txt Eli attached. High-level: the handshake failures look like a client cert validation error originating from our outbound TLS stack when Redwood POSTs to FastPay's endpoint. Two possibilities:

1) FastPay's cert chain is missing an intermediate CA on the endpoint (common in ephemeral staging envs).
2) There's an SNI mismatch if the callback uses an IP address rather than hostname in the cert.

If FastPay can confirm the following I can narrow it down:
- The exact callback URL being registered (scheme/host:port/path)
- The public cert chain (PEM) for that endpoint or a curl -v output showing the TLS handshake

ETA: once we get the above, I can reproduce and propose a fix within 1-2 business days. If it's an intermediate CA, FastPay will need to correct the cert; if it's SNI we'll patch our routing to use the hostname. Either way, pairing session would speed it to same day.

Happy to jump on a quick call — I'm available today 1–3pm PT or Monday morning.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
